description.p: npad is a native Linux text editor built with Rust and GTK4, using a hand-written editor widget instead of an embedded Scintilla view.

It opens files in multiple tabs, highlights their syntax with syntect for more than thirty languages, and offers a regular-expression capable find and replace engine with case sensitivity, wrap-around and replace-all support.

Buffers are stored in a ropey rope with a structured undo and redo stack, and encoding and line endings are handled transparently for UTF-8, UTF-16 and GBK files, including byte order marks and CRLF endings.
The editor restores your last session, remembers your preferences, and switches between a light and a dark theme.
First MVP release: self-drawn GTK4 editor core, syntax highlighting, regular-expression find and replace, encoding and line-ending handling, session restore and light/dark themes.
